title: A peek inside the Colonna Palace, Rome's most exclusive tourist site
establishes: The Colonna are described as part of the Black Nobility, the Roman families that remained loyal to the Pope after the capture of Rome in 1870, and the family's palace remains privately held and inhabited.
doesNotEstablish: A current secret council, occult command structure or control of the Vatican, Italy or world affairs.

title: Origins and Characteristics
establishes: Vatican City State was created by the Lateran Treaty of 1929 to secure the independence of the Holy See.
doesNotEstablish: That Roman aristocratic families secretly own or command the Holy See.

title: Lateran Pacts of 11 February 1929
establishes: The legal settlement of the Roman Question and creation of Vatican sovereignty, including the financial convention between Italy and the Holy See.
doesNotEstablish: A hereditary aristocratic command structure above the treaty parties.

title: Orsini
establishes: The Orsini are a major Roman family documented from the late tenth century, historically linked to popes, cardinals, senators, territorial power and rivalry with the Colonna.
doesNotEstablish: Unbroken control from antiquity, a modern secret command role or occult allegiance.

title: Colonna
establishes: The Colonna are a documented Roman family from the twelfth century with major medieval territorial, ecclesiastical and political influence.
doesNotEstablish: Current control of the papacy, Italian state or global institutions.

title: The Colonna Family
establishes: The family's documented nine-century continuity, palace ownership, papal and military history, and long conflict with the Orsini.
doesNotEstablish: That cultural and property continuity equals secret political sovereignty.

title: Borghese
establishes: The Borghese rose from Siena into the highest Roman nobility after Camillo Borghese became Pope Paul V, with wealth and offices distributed to relatives.
doesNotEstablish: A current unified Borghese command network or occult role.

title: Caetani
establishes: The Caetani have documented medieval branches and gained exceptional power through Benedetto Caetani, Pope Boniface VIII, papal offices and territorial acquisitions.
doesNotEstablish: A continuous hidden government or present-day collective control.

title: Massimo
establishes: The Massimo are documented in medieval Rome; claims of descent from the ancient Fabii are not supported by certain documentation.
doesNotEstablish: Ancient Roman bloodline continuity or secret global authority.

title: Massimo, princes of Arsoli
establishes: Archival records for the Roman Massimo family from the medieval period onward and explicitly distinguishes legendary ancestry from documented history.
doesNotEstablish: Literal descent from ancient Roman patricians or a modern occult bloodline.

title: Chigi
establishes: The Chigi originated as Sienese bankers, entered Roman papal nobility, gained imperial and territorial titles and held major ecclesiastical offices.
doesNotEstablish: Current command of conclaves, the Vatican or world finance.

title: Aldobrandini
establishes: The Aldobrandini were a Florentine noble family transferred to Rome and elevated through Pope Clement VIII and papal-family patronage.
doesNotEstablish: An uninterrupted modern family command structure.

title: Odescalchi
establishes: The Odescalchi rose from Como and were transferred into Roman high nobility after an Odescalchi became Pope Innocent XI.
doesNotEstablish: Current covert control or a continuous ancient bloodline.

title: Torlonia
establishes: The Torlonia were a comparatively recent banking and landholding dynasty whose Roman princely status developed in the nineteenth century.
doesNotEstablish: Ancient bloodline status or membership in a timeless ruling council.

title: Boncompagni
establishes: The Boncompagni rose through Pope Gregory XIII and later inherited Ludovisi titles and property through marriage.
doesNotEstablish: A surviving modern command role above church or state institutions.

title: Pamphili
establishes: The Pamphili rose through Pope Innocent X; their property and succession later passed into Doria Landi and Borghese Aldobrandini lines.
doesNotEstablish: A single pure bloodline or uninterrupted family command.

title: Emanuele Ruspoli, prince of Poggio Suasa
establishes: Emanuele Ruspoli represented the pro-unification 'white nobility', demonstrating that Roman aristocratic families did not form one papal-loyal bloc after 1870.
doesNotEstablish: That all noble houses belong to the Black Nobility or share a common political programme.

publisher: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops
title: Isaiah 14 — Morning Star note
establishes: Isaiah 14 addresses a king of Babylon; the Latin term Lucifer was later applied in Christian interpretation to Satan.
doesNotEstablish: That light, Venus or morning-star symbolism proves modern Luciferian worship.

title: The Gods and Goddesses of Canaan
establishes: Baal's documented place within the ancient Canaanite religious world as a storm and warrior deity.
doesNotEstablish: Continuity into one modern elite cult or a relationship with the listed families.

title: Moloch — Oxford Handbook of Biblical Monsters
establishes: Scholarly dispute over whether mōlek referred to a deity, a sacrificial rite or related practices.
doesNotEstablish: Literal modern ritual activity by any named family or institution.

title: Kronos / Saturn collection record
establishes: Classical mythology and later associations of Kronos/Saturn with agriculture, the planet and time.
doesNotEstablish: A unified Saturnian command system behind modern institutions.
